blocks.x: What Applied AI & GenAI changes inside Energy & Utilities: the processes we target, the controls we inherit, the platforms underneath, and the measured delta at every gate.

In Energy & Utilities, applied ai & generative ai at dataq soft covers the full lifecycle of enterprise intelligence: strategy and value mapping, platform build-out, model adaptation, retrieval architectures, multimodal systems, and the governance fabric that keeps every model auditable. That is the baseline pattern; the differentiator is what it connects to: enterprise ai strategy & roadmapping, generative ai platform engineering, llm fine-tuning & model operations — delivered on Dataq Compass and Dataq Forge and Dataq Nexus with the sector's regulatory posture built in.

items: Renewable supply and flexible demand make legacy forecasting blind; imbalance costs and curtailment climb while forecasts run on yesterday's methods.
IT/OT convergence, remote access growth and legacy SCADA estates create attack paths with physical consequences; CIP/NIS2 duties expand faster than programs mature.
Turbines, transformers and pipelines hold decades of life left — and zero telemetry. Condition-based maintenance is impossible without sensing, and failures cost the most when they are unscheduled.

blocks.x: Two regimes anchor the control design here: CSRD / ISSB and NERC CIP (North America). Critical-infrastructure protection standards for bulk power systems. Evidence for both is generated by the delivery itself — control tests, replay trails and documentation are artifacts of the program, not a reconstruction project.

Delivery runs on one weekly rhythm for every program of this type. Weeks 1–2 are measurement only: we lock the current metric with your team and both sides sign it before a line of build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver a bounded pilot — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a named control owner on your side. Weeks 9–12 turn what worked into runbooks, monitoring and enablement, then report the measured delta against the baseline. A missed gate means a documented stop-or-redirect decision, not a quiet extension.
